validity.researcher_notes: Confirmed independently (this shard was drafted before comparing notes with the parallel P2649 shard, which reaches the identical conclusion from the same primary documents -- convergent, not circular). Three FERC Federal Register notices under Docket No. CP15-504-000 (Dominion Carolina Gas Transmission, LLC) all describe the SAME project as 'approximately 28-mile[s]' / 'approximately 28 miles of new 8-inch-diameter... pipeline': Notice of Application (2015-15092, 2015-06-19), Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review (2015-31720, 2015-12-17), and the EA Notice of Availability (2016-04143, 2016-02-26). 28 mi x 1.60934 = 45.06 km -- an essentially exact match to P2649's recorded 45.00 km. Meanwhile the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook ('Historical Projects (1996-2024)' tab) carries exactly ONE database record for this same Docket CP15-504 project -- Operator 'Dominion Carolina Gas Transmission', Project Name 'Columbia to Eastover Pipeline', Miles=29, Diameter=8in, Additional Capacity=18 MMcf/d, Cost=$36M, Completed Date=2016-11-01 -- and the Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Planned Projects in the Americas' (Nov. 2016 PDF) independently repeats the identical 29-mile/South Carolina/2016-completion/18-MMcf/d figures, matching P4381's recorded 29 mi almost exactly. Every other attribute (owner, capacity, completion year, diameter, state) is identical across both rows. The 1-mile gap (28 vs 29 mi, 3.6%) reads as a proposed-vs-as-built mileage refinement on ONE line, not two pipelines -- no FERC document, EIA record, or trade-press mention anywhere in this search describes a second Columbia-to-Eastover-area pipeline, a second CP-docket, or a second capacity/purpose distinct from the one 18,000-Dth/d (=18 MMcf/d) firm-service delivery to the International Paper plant in Eastover, SC.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Sheet's LastUpdated for this row is 2022-09-27. The newest evidence found that names THIS specific 29-mile Columbia-to-Eastover lateral by name is still the 2016 in-service filing (see Status/Start fills) -- no post-2018 document specific to this segment was located this pass. However, two pieces of dated evidence support continuity past LastUpdated: (1) EIA's same workbook records a separate, more recent CGT-system project on the SAME operator's network -- the 'Moore-Dorchester Optimization Project' (Docket CP22-181, Completed Date 2022-09-30, Operator 'Carolina Gas Transmission', +10 MMcf/d) -- almost exactly contemporaneous with this row's LastUpdated (2022-09-27), independent confirmation that the parent CGT system was actively operating and investing in capacity as of September 2022, not idle or divested; (2) the current owner's corporate site (bhegts.com/our-businesses/CGT, accessed 2026-09-10 -- four years newer than LastUpdated) describes the whole CGT system, of which this lateral is a permanent physical part, in the present tense as an operating ~1,500-mile interstate pipeline serving 150+ delivery points, with no mention of any lateral being idled, abandoned, or retired. This is a short (29 mi), small-diameter (8in) firm-service delivery lateral built for one large industrial customer (the International Paper plant in Eastover, SC) under a FERC-approved negotiated-rate transportation contract -- exactly the class of asset that, once in FERC tariff service, has no natural retirement trigger short of the customer closing or relocating, and no search this pass (FERC dockets, EIA, SEC EDGAR full-text) turned up any indication of the Eastover IP plant closing or this lateral being abandoned. Verdict is 'confirm' on the balance of this circumstantial-but-multi-sourced continuity evidence; tier flagged medium (not high) because the newest evidence naming THIS specific segment by name predates LastUpdated.
